newsItems.title: Tanvi Khanna Stages Epic Comeback to Win Mumbai PSA Title
newsItems.excerpt: The HCL-SRFI PSA Challenger Squash Tournament in Mumbai crowned its champions Friday, July 3, at the Juhu Vile Parle Gymkhana Club in a day of dramatic finishes. India's Tanvi Khanna, the third seed, looked headed for defeat when she dropped the opening two games 8-11, 2-11 to Egypt's second seed Farida Walid, but the world No. 74 dug deep to win the next three 12-10, 11-9, 11-7 in 54 minutes and claim her fifth PSA title in 11 final appearances. Khanna credited coach Dhruv Dhawan for urging her to play longer rallies rather than force winners when she was struggling at the front of the court. In the men's final, Malaysia's Mohammad Syafiq Kamal overturned a two-game deficit of his own to beat Yassin Shohdy 6-11, 9-11, 11-8, 14-12, 11-8, denying the Egyptian who had eliminated top seed Velavan Senthilkumar in the semifinals. The $30,000 combined event delivered a memorable double for Asian squash.

newsItems.title: Lee Zii Jia Ends Two-Year Wait for Canada Open Semifinal
newsItems.excerpt: Malaysia's Lee Zii Jia finally has a breakthrough to show for his injury comeback after reaching the YONEX Canada Open semifinals with a commanding 21-15, 21-13 quarterfinal victory over Chinese Taipei's sixth seed Wang Po-Wei on Friday, July 3, at the Markham Pan Am Centre. The world No. 60 needed just 34 minutes to dispatch Po-Wei, backing up straight-game wins over Liao Jhuo-Fu and a first-round walkover when Kidambi Srikanth retired, and reached his first World Tour semifinal since winning the Australian Open in June 2024. It is also his first semi since claiming Olympic bronze at Paris 2024. Lee will face Japan's Riki Takei on Saturday, July 4, in a rematch of their Australian Open qualifying clash last month, which the Malaysian won 15-21, 21-17, 21-16. A title run at the $250,000 BWF Super 300 could lift Lee back toward the world's top 50 after an injury-hit spell that dropped him outside the top 100 earlier this year.

newsItems.title: Tokyo Open Finals Day Pits Fujiwara Against Kao for Gold
newsItems.excerpt: The PPA Asia 500 Sansan Tokyo Open reaches championship day Saturday, July 4, at Arena Tachikawa Tachihi in the Japanese capital's first PPA Tour Asia stop. Rika Fujiwara, who captured Japan's first PPA Asia singles gold at Macau in May, demolished Lingwei Kong 11-1, 11-5 in the women's singles semifinals to set up a final against Pei Chuan Kao, who rallied past Kiora Kunimoto 9-11, 11-9, 12-10. Fujiwara also reached the women's doubles final with 15-year-old partner Kyo Sawaki after beating Yufei Long and Andy Dicosabrevich. In men's singles, Australia's Mitchell Hargreaves recovered from a game down to beat Nasa Hatakeyama 5-11, 11-8, 12-10 and will face Hong Kit Wong, who defeated Zane Ford 11-6, 12-10. The men's doubles final features Japan's Yuta Funemizu and 15-year-old Tama Shimabukuro against Collin Johns and Len Yang after the home pair edged Eunggwon Kim and Wong 12-10, 6-11, 11-5. Medal matches across all five pro disciplines cap the $50,000 event that drew more than 800 players.

newsItems.title: Wang and Sun Reach Mixed Doubles Final as China's Men Exit
newsItems.excerpt: The WTT United States Smash 2026 delivered contrasting fortunes for China's table tennis stars on Friday, July 3, at the Ontario Convention Center in Southern California. Wang Chuqin and Sun Yingsha swept Brazil's Hugo Calderano and Bruna Takahashi 11-9, 11-4, 11-6 in the mixed doubles semifinals, booking a final spot after surviving a 3-2 quarterfinal scare against Alexis Lebrun and Satsuki Odo when they trailed by two games. Hours later, defending men's singles champion Wang Chuqin fell 11-13, 2-11, 11-8, 7-11 to Denmark's Anders Lind in the Round of 16, and Lin Shidong lost to Alexis Lebrun, completing a wipeout that left China with no men in the singles quarterfinals. On the women's side, Kuai Man finally broke through against Shin Yubin with a 3-0 win — 11-8, 11-8, 13-11 — for her first career victory over the Korean, while Sun Yingsha earlier beat Nina Mittelham 11-9, 11-3, 11-6. American No. 1 Kanak Jha remains the host nation's last men's singles hope at the $1.55 million Grand Smash, which runs through Sunday, July 5.
